proposal:
STATUS. LQC-GF2 is hand-derived and unexecuted; nothing here was run. It is a polynomial preprocessor and certificate rule, not polynomial SAT, and gives no universal growth bound. The watcher handoff contributes nothing.

CERTIFICATE. Normalise, deduplicate and group clauses by exact support K (width c_K, forbidden set P_K, m_K=|P_K|). The certificate is M in GF(2)^(r x n), R in GF(2)^(n x r) with r<n, and per block an index set J_K of size d_K, a local right inverse R_K and a duplicate-free quotient set Q_K in GF(2)^(J_K). Checks:
C1. MR=I_r.
C2. Rows M_j (j in J_K) vanish outside K; their restriction M_K satisfies M_K R_K=I.
C3. M_K p lies in Q_K for every p in P_K.
C4. m_K=|Q_K|*2^(c_K-d_K).

Lemma LQC (hand proof). By C2, v -> (M_K v, v+R_K M_K v) is a bijection onto GF(2)^(d_K) x ker M_K, so every fibre has size 2^(c_K-d_K). C3 gives P_K inside the preimage of Q_K, and C4 gives equal cardinality, so they are equal. Hence x violates block K iff (Mx)_(J_K) is in Q_K. So F(x)=G(Mx) for all x, where G forbids Q_K on J_K. C1 gives G(y)=F(Ry), so F and G are equisatisfiable with lift y -> Ry. No 2^n, 2^r or 2^(c_K) term appears.

BUDGETS (bit operations; L = total literal count).
- Check: r^2*n for C1, plus sum of m_K*c_K*d_K for C2-C4.
- Arithmetic: GF(2) bits and counters below 2m. No rationals or HNF.
- Certificate size: at most 2rn + sum(c_K*d_K + |Q_K|*d_K) bits.
- Quotient: r<n variables, sum of m_K/2^(s_K) <= m clauses, widths d_K <= c_K.

DISCOVERY (GF(2) elimination only).
D1. The stabiliser S_K lies inside P_K+p_0, so there are only m_K candidates. Test P_K+v inside P_K by lookup: m_K^2*c_K. Also s_K <= log2 m_K.
D2. Annihilator basis L_K by nullspace: c_K^3.
D3. Stack all L_K (N <= L rows). One elimination gives rank r, basis rows, the relation matrix D, and R from pivot columns: N*n*r.
D4. Adapted basis: greedy attempt, else the FR-kappa fallback below.
Total is O(mL + L*n^2). This replaces chosen-span enumeration and exhaustive right-inverse search. D4 is not complete.

RESIDUAL. T_total <= poly(L) + T_solver(G). G is arbitrary, because every CNF on r variables is the quotient of its pair-lift. Residual work is therefore not bounded by this method.

FR-KAPPA (my 00055 idea, read as: overcomplete frame with kappa=N-r relations). With a non-adapted basis, block K depends on y through a d_K x |U_K| matrix T_K, where U_K is the set of basis variables it touches. LQC extends: replace J_K by T_K, require T_K*M supported in K and locally right-invertible, and let G forbid the preimage of Q_K under T_K. That costs |Q_K|*2^(e_K) clauses of width |U_K|, with e_K=|U_K|-d_K. So FR-kappa helps exactly when e_K=O(log L), i.e. incompatible spaces with short relations. It does not help with:
(i) extra clauses: odd m_K forces s_K=0, the block space is full and r=n for every basis;
(ii) long relations, or choosing a basis that minimises max e_K;
(iii) residual hardness.

PADDING LEMMA (hand proof, negative). Take any 3-CNF Phi. Replace each clause C_j by a block on (a,b,c,t_j) with fresh t_j: forbid all 8 points with t_j=1, plus the one point with t_j=0 that falsifies C_j. The core has s=3 and |R|=1<4, so Lemma S of 00056 recovers it. Then G is the conjunction of (not t_j) and Z=Phi. So the RC-FT test 'Z SAT' is SAT itself, mu=#MUS(Z) is not polynomially computable in general, and the T93 gap problem at s=3 is NP-complete. Extra-clause robustness beyond restricted Z is equivalent to general SAT.

FALSIFIABLE LARGER CASES (not run).
A_r, n=2r in {16,24,32}. Put y_i=x_(2i-1) xor x_(2i). Clauses: (y_i or not y_(i+1)) cyclically for i=1..r, plus (not y_1 or not y_(r/2+1)). Each lifts to 4 width-4 clauses, so m=4r+4. Predictions:
- every block has s=d=2;
- D3 rank is exactly r and the basis is adapted;
- LQC accepts;
- the quotient has r variables and r+1 binary clauses, SAT with all y=0;
- check cost is at most r^2*n+32(r+1), which is 8,736 bit operations at n=32, against 2^32 enumeration.
Refutation: any mismatch of F(x)=G(Mx) under brute force at n=16 or 24, or under sampling at n=32.

B_T, n=6T in {18,24,30}. Per triangle, pair-sum forms a,b,c. Blocks: parity a xor b=0 (8 clauses on 4 variables), lifted (a or c), lifted (not b or not c). Links: lifted (c_t or a_(t+1)). So m=20T-4. Predictions:
- No adapted basis exists. It would need a+b, two forms spanning span(a,c) and two spanning span(b,c); those pairs share at most span(c), giving at least 4 elements in rank 3. Any correct compatibility test must fail.
- FR-kappa with e=1 gives 3T variables and 5T-1 binary clauses, SAT.
- T=2 (12 variables, 36 clauses) fits v2. I predict a skip for incompatibility, not for odd blocks. I make no peak prediction.
missing_theorem:
T94 (first; Lean, general n, no sorry). Lemma LQC including the T_K form: C1-C4 imply F(x)=G(Mx) for all x and G(y)=F(Ry) for all y. The proof must be compositional:
(a) a fibre-counting lemma for GF(2)-linear maps with an explicit right inverse;
(b) a support-restriction lemma;
(c) list induction over blocks.
Instance proofs then check only C1-C4 by kernel decide, with size linear in the certificate. The existing CompressionSoundness.lean covers complete enumeration only. None of this is machine-checked.

T95 (discovery completeness, open). A polynomial algorithm deciding whether subspaces A_1..A_m of GF(2)^n admit a common adapted basis, or, for FR-kappa, finding a basis that minimises max e_K. I recall this is equivalent to the generated subspace lattice being distributive; that is from memory and not rechecked. Without T95, a greedy skip cannot be told apart from true non-existence. The auto00008 skip is unclassified in this sense.

T96 (arbitrary extra clauses). By the padding lemma, an unconditional extra-clause theorem would be polynomial SAT itself. The provable target is conditional: if |R_K|<2^(s_K-1) and Z has fibre primal treewidth at most k, then G and H together are decidable in 2^O(k)*poly(L). This is unproved and is explicitly family detection.
self_attack:
1. LQC soundness is elementary. It lifts the 12-variable cap for certificate checking only. No hard instance gets easier, since the residual G is arbitrary.
2. The padding lemma undercuts my own 00056: the Z test and mu are NP-hard in general. The matched fixture there says nothing about this.
3. C4 is unsound if P_K or Q_K contains duplicates, so distinctness must be checked by sorting. Clauses subsumed across different supports are not merged, so discovery can miss stabilisers. That is incompleteness, not unsoundness.
4. D4 greedy remains incomplete. FR-kappa substitution is exponential in e_K and needs a cap, which brings back skips.
5. Kernel decide on r^2*n matrix bits at n=32 may exceed the 45-second budget. This is untested and may need row-wise lemmas.
6. Stabiliser structure is brittle: one added point destroys it. Gap recovery covers additions with |R|<2^(s-1) only, not deletions.
7. The A_r and B_T numbers are hand arithmetic. The T=2 skip prediction depends on v2 internals I have not seen.
8. The padding argument is a hand proof. It was not checked in Lean.
mechanism_signature: LQC-GF2 | unimplemented | certificate (M, R, {T_K, R_K, Q_K}) | checks: MR=I, local support, local right inverse, membership, cardinality m_K=|Q_K|*2^(c_K-d_K) | no 2^n, 2^r or 2^c enumeration | discovery: m_K stabiliser candidates, nullspace, one stacked elimination | FR-kappa fallback costs 2^(e_K) | padding lemma: extra-clause robustness = SAT | residual solver unbounded | adapted-basis completeness open
delta_from_prior:
00056 gave a block-local rule that still enumerated 2^(c_K) local points, with an invertible frame, and proposed Z-SAT and mu as the robustness criteria.

New here:
(1) The cardinality check C4 removes local 2^(c_K) tables; the certificate is polynomial in encoded length for unbounded width.
(2) Explicit GF(2) discovery with separate bit-operation budgets, using the m_K-candidate stabiliser trick and a right inverse from pivots.
(3) An exact cost boundary for FR-kappa: 2^(e_K) per block. It helps with incompatibility and never with odd blocks.
(4) The padding lemma: it settles the T93 gap problem at s=3 as NP-complete and withdraws Z-SAT and mu as polynomial criteria.
(5) Family B_T, where incompatibility is provable rather than a greedy artefact.
(6) T94 as a compositional Lean target.

Not new: adapted-frame discovery (T91, now T95) is still open; nonlinear structure, auto00008 and any universal bound are untouched.
